Melbourne as a Global Cultural Destination01Executive summary

Melbourne's cultural offer is compelling and drives significant economic benefits, but its position is being challenged

MELBOURNE
CULTURAL PULSE · 2015
01Compelling offer
>10m
Australian and international visitors attracted by the city in 2015
Cultural experiences are the second most common reason for visiting, after seeing friends.
03Seen as creative
69%
of visitors think the city is “creative”
World's highest concentration of live music venues; Museum Victoria attracts 3x the audience of the National Museum of Australia.
02Economic benefit
~$23b
contributed to the State economy by creative industries and cultural tourism in 2015
8% of Victorian employment (2013). Cultural visitors stay 25% longer and spend 20% more per trip.
04Global index
12th
of 38 cultural and creative cities on the global Performance Index
1st in Australia · 3rd in Asia. London, New York and Paris hold the top three positions.
POSITION CHALLENGED
International visitors name Sydney first. NSW plans $600m of projects; WA invested $430m in the New Museum for WA.
Source: BCG, Melbourne as a Global Cultural Destination, Executive Summary (1/3). Global Traveller Survey, October 2016 (2,457 adults). Melbourne as a Global Cultural Destination03Performance Index

Five metrics measure a city's attractiveness as a global cultural and creative destination

INDEX
CITY
ATTRACTIVENESS
score out of 60
Creative workforce
% workforce in cultural and creative industries
Quality of experiences
% excellent reviews on TripAdvisor
Expert recognition
# times listed in expert 'Top' lists
Social buzz
social media “buzz” score
Traveller perception
Cultural Traveller Survey ranking
How a city is scored
1
Measure five KPIs
The five metrics, for each of 38 cities globally.
2
Score against the best
The best-in-class city for each KPI receives the maximum score of 20; every other city is scored relative to it.
3
Weight and sum
KPI scores are weighted and summed into one overall score.
4
Rank the cities
Overall score out of 60 sets each city's position on the Performance Index.
Result for Melbourne
27of 60→12thof 38 cities
Dimensions A–D carry the five metrics (metric 1 spans A and B); E and F (outer ring) carry no metrics: they less directly relate to the city's attractiveness for creative professionals and cultural visitors. Cultural Traveller Survey: over 1,000 respondents from ten key future markets ranked their top 10 cultural and creative destinations. Melbourne result from p.17–18. Source: BCG analysis.INDEPENDENT REDESIGN · 05 / 12

Melbourne as a Global Cultural Destination06Strategic priorities

Five strategic priorities to improve Melbourne's cultural offer

MELBOURNE
CULTURAL SYSTEM
1 · AwarenessMake culture a key part of the Melbourne proposition
1aDevelop clear creative city messages
1bTarget priority segments and travellers
1cGrow creative city awareness through investment, multi-faceted strategy (incl. social media)
2 · ProtectProtect existing infrastructure
2aExpand supply of creative spaces in under-served areas, address affordability
2bImprove maintenance, utilisation and storage of assets
3 · OptimiseOptimise the current offer
3aBuild an integrated marketing, sales, reviews platform for creative and cultural activities
3bEnhance connectivity between attractions
4 · ExpandExpand our offer
4aUpgrade and invest in new programming
4bUpgrade and invest in new infrastructure to fill gaps
5 · GovernEnhance governance
5aUse the Evaluation Framework to assess impact, viability and feasibility to build a pipeline of investments
5bStrengthen governance of Melbourne Arts Precinct
5cImprove agency collaboration
Five priorities, one system: awareness at the core, governance as the outer ring. Together they may lift Melbourne's position on the Performance Index.
The five priorities build on the Creative State Strategy. Labels follow the source; short tags (Awareness, Protect, Optimise, Expand, Govern) follow the executive summary wording. Source: BCG analysis.INDEPENDENT REDESIGN · 11 / 12
Melbourne as a Global Cultural Destination06Strategic priorities

Ideas should be compared against a three-part Evaluation Framework, which can support a 10-year pipeline

Gate A · 5 questions
Desirability
Measured by the Performance Index
Does the idea make Melbourne a more attractive place for people to study and work in?
Does the idea enhance consumer perception of the quality of Melbourne's cultural and creative offer?
Does the idea enhance expert perception of the quality of Melbourne's cultural and creative offer?
Does the idea make Melbourne more attractive for locals and international tourists to visit?
Does the idea enhance Melbourne's international brand recognition and strength?
Gate B · 2 questions
Viability
 
Does the idea provide an acceptable economic return?
Does the idea provide important non-economic benefits?
Gate C · 1 question
Feasibility
 
Is the idea technically, administratively and politically feasible?
Outcome
10-year pipeline of investments
Links to priority 5a: use the Evaluation Framework to assess impact, viability and feasibility to build a pipeline of investments.
